figures.finding: Pic Portugal's Cash Rebate pays 25% of eligible spend in Portugal, up to 30% on the Cultural Test, with a minimum spend of EUR 500,000 for fiction or animation and EUR 200,000 for documentary or post-production, up to EUR 1.5 million a project, from a 2024 pot of up to EUR 14 million in two application rounds a year.

figures.applies: Portugal, national and foreign film, TV and VOD productions, 2024 to 2025 rules.

figures.finding: Pic Portugal's Cash Refund, for spend in Portugal of EUR 2.5 million or more, reimburses 30% of the first EUR 2 million and up to 25% of the rest, up to EUR 6 million a work and EUR 3 million an episode, from an annual budget of up to EUR 20 million, first come first served, paid in one instalment the year after final recognition.
figures.applies: Portugal, higher-budget fiction, animation and documentary, from 2024.

sources.said: With an annual budget of up to 20 million euros, the Pic Portugal – Cash Refund Incentive is geared towards higher-budget productions, with eligible expenditure in the national territory equal to or greater than 2.5 million euros per project. … The Cash Refund consists of a reimbursement of 30% on the first 2 million euros and up to 25% on the excess. … This support can go up to 6 million euros for cinematographic and audiovisual works, with a limit of 3 million euros per episode.

figures.finding: ICA, the Portuguese Film and Audiovisual Institute, runs more than twenty selective support schemes (development, production, distribution and more), grants 90% or more of film production money on a selective basis with emphasis on first and second films, and had about EUR 20.6 million for them in 2019.

value.fund: ICA – Instituto do Cinema e do Audiovisual subsidy schemes
value.selectiveShare: 90% or more of film production money

figures.applies: Portugal, Portuguese film and TV projects; budget figure for 2019.

sources.said: The ICA manages more than twenty support (subsidy) schemes, including: development (film and TV); production (film and TV), distribution, exhibition, festivals, film literacy, promotion, etc. … 90% or more of the available amount for film production is granted on a selective basis. Emphasis is put on supporting first/second films by new directors. Yearly budget (2019) for the subsidy schemes: ca. € 20,6 million.
